title: Sharpen compiler width divisors with exact plateau visit counts (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration: sharpen the plateau-product divisor for the separated chronological compiler of CubeJerry's [#7424](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7424). This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
old exponent on every plateau: tau = A*ceil(log2 k_min)
new exact maximum visits:     nu = 1+floor((min(N,A*gamma_next-1)-A*gamma)/delta)
uniform consequence:          nu <= A-1 < tau

B_n divides product_gamma S(gamma)^nu_gamma, for every n <= N.
```

Here delta is the smallest positive fresh-source rank on the plateau. Paid exits always leave that plateau; each complement step inside it subtracts at least delta. Applying the exact visit count to every prime-valuation chain proves the smaller divisor. The new divisor divides the old one, strictly whenever an observed plateau has source count greater than one.

For A=64, N=127, targets (2,3) and one paid rank-1 site, the upper divisor decreases from 2^64 to the attained 2^32. The width formula is credited prior work in #7424; the new result is the general bound. No new kappa or changed width sequence is claimed.

Only seven new files in `research/additive-plateau-width/`. [Written proof](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/75aa393e808d030930879b87815e0abb7bb5742d/research/additive-plateau-width/PROOF.md), [reproduction and scope](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/blob/75aa393e808d030930879b87815e0abb7bb5742d/research/additive-plateau-width/README.md), [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19571833). The formal-interface-lemma card changes scope to this compiler-size side result. Canonical base is e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57, priority revision 8, selected #7000.

Credit CubeJerry #7424 at d622d8c62defa9defeb95741e88b33a120044866 and #7345 for the numerical library; codyw912 #4638 for the original plateau-product divisor; mihir-s-05 #4507/#5071 for chronological gcd/LCM batching; zxv, jacobalansussman, pinterbanget, 1337isnot1337 and the retained compiler/native lineage. Their results are cited premises. No predecessor scientific suite was replayed.

## Evidence

- Before: the common exponent is A*ceil(log2 k_min). After: each plateau has its exact additive visit maximum, always at most A-1. The all-prime divisor proof retains individual chronological cuts and permits primes outside the rank alphabet.
- Local CPython 3.12.15 normal and optimized checks pass 670 distinct rule/maximum fixtures, 11,926 width rows and 851 plateau rows. Every literal graph maximum equals the new visit count; 448 divisors are strictly smaller and 222 fixtures contain only base ranks. Another 294 truncated first-plateau fixtures attain the divisor. Sixteen explicit domain/semantic controls pass.
- Both timed VERIFY.json commands complete in about 0.05 seconds, below their 120-second limits. Registered replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed`; the direct marker is `PASS_ADDITIVE_PLATEAU_WIDTH`.
- Metadata/pins, warning-strict in-memory source compilation, committed bytes/executable modes/source history, official export integrity/input coverage, and an optimized read-only Git-free exported replay with PATH=/nonexistent pass locally. Receipts are computed and bound to source hashes; no receipt is hand-written.

From the worktree root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/additive-plateau-width/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -O -W error -B research/additive-plateau-width/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/additive-plateau-width
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/additive-plateau-width --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Any CPython 3.12 path can replace the local interpreter path. The standard library suffices. The direct verifier needs no predecessor checkout or network. SOURCES.json identifies the pending source's exact proof and citation hash as mathematical provenance; it is not an executable dependency or a runtime theorem-authentication claim.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal result rests on the written proof and the credited separated-flow premises: r_max<k_min, m<=A, constant plateau census, individual chronological exits and unit base widths. Finite enumeration corroborates it. The executable checker bounds A,N to 256 and each explicit role list to four entries.

This improves an upper divisor and bit envelope. It supplies no new asymptotic degree, evaluated selected manifest, batching algorithm, native instruction stream, physical memory/runtime gain or complete multiplication theorem. The explicit-output obstruction in #7424 survives. All five selected assumptions remain. Native semantics, owner erasure, precision/tape and analytic obligations were not run or discharged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No selected cold replay, Lean or Docker was run; no local check was deferred to CI.

## Open next questions

1. Retain actual source multiplicities and gcd discounts for one evaluated selected histogram. Begin with its exact chronological source manifest and a prime-valuation recurrence; both are absent here.
2. Specify a compact width representation and exact divisibility-query cost when A varies. A smaller upper divisor does not remove the cited quadratic explicit-output obstruction.

## Related open work

- [#7424](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7424): direct predecessor and source of the ambient-constant question. This refines its plateau exponent; the attaining cap-one width agrees with its cited formula.
- [#7345](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7345): constructs quantitative default-ambient numerical libraries. The new proof bounds their divisors through the independent-ambient extension; it changes no table-generation algorithm.
- [#7178](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/7178): proves multiplicative-shell counting sharpness for an adaptive compiler. This result concerns visits within a default-height plateau. It does not use or extend that shell theorem, count a smaller shell language, or prove gcd cancellation.

The completion overlap check read this account's six other open PRs created since the CLAIM: #7461, #7462, #7463, #7465, #7466 and #7467. They study different objects or quantities. None computes this chronological width divisor or plateau visit count, so no additional related-work line or numerical comparison is warranted.

## CI notes

```text
test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record
AssertionError: '`make frontier7000-verify`' not found
FAILED (failures=1, skipped=24)
```

The actual job log shows that the CI verification document's current section still describes #6030 and `make frontier6030-verify`. Direct inspection of canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57` confirms that its selected record instead names `make frontier7000-verify`. This PR changes neither document nor the test; its exact diff contains only the seven new package files. The [package replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/43279626746/job/131399864584) was skipped after plan failed. No hosted job executed this package.
